Forecast Discussion

High pressure extends over the Southeast U.S. today as a backdoor cold front nudges southward toward the Mason-Dixon line. This setup will promote sunshine and unseasonable warmth across the Southern Appalachians through Thursday.

The backdoor front will get just close enough for a stray shower by Thursday afternoon across Southwest Virginia. Near-record warm weather continues on Thursday.

Changes begin on Friday as we anticipate another very warm day, but with a few showers arriving by late-day, continuing into Friday night. This will be driven by a strong cold front crossing the region, and signaling the arrival of a much cooler fall air mass.

This weekend, temperatures will actually run below normal for a change, with frost and/or freeze potential by daybreak Sunday. More valley frost is likely by daybreak Monday as well.

Accompanying the chill will be generally clear skies, so it will feel and look like autumn, but also be conducive to the many outdoor activities and festivals going on across WNC and SW VA.
